papers.abstract_en: Commitment services, such as timestamping, transparency logs and provenance registries, let a party prove that it bound itself to a record without publishing the record. Today an operator runs them, or a blockchain replaces the operator at the cost of network-wide agreement on every write. We present Cambium, a permissioned peer-to-peer service in which participants build each cycle's commitment root together, so that no single party decides which inputs the root includes. Fixed-size committees certify inputs and use a recursive-doubling merge, in which disjoint groups recompute every intermediate value, to spread root construction across all participants. A successful cycle costs each node $O(c\log(n/c))$ messages for committee size $c$, and each node stores its own $O(\log(n/c))$ proof per cycle, along with the $O(n)$ membership roster. A Go prototype on AWS with $c=4$, 8-256 nodes and simulated stragglers completes cycles in 12-148 ms and verifies proofs in under 1.5 ms, and demonstrates logarithmic growth. We show that conflicting certificates identify their signers, that a proof binds a signed input to its root, and that two conflicting roots both become final only if at least a third of the nodes are Byzantine, except with probability exponentially small in the number of committees. We also set out the membership, proof-availability and exclusion questions a community deploying Cambium must answer.

papers.abstract_en: This paper proposes a Square-root Atomic Norm Minimization (SR-ANM) estimator for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation in the single measurement vector (SMV) setting. This new framework, inspired by the Square-root Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (Square-root LASSO), relies on a residual term based on the $L_{2}$-norm rather than the usual squared $L_{2}$-norm so as to obtain an estimator whereby the hyperparameter of the atomic norm in the unconstrained convex optimization problem exhibits robustness to the noise level compared to classical ANM. Experimental verification across a wide signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) range from 0 dB to 40 dB using the the probability of detection and the angular root-mean-squared error (RMSE) confirms the increased noise robustness of the proposed framework compared to ANM.

papers.abstract_en: We consider the offline generation of coordinated paths for N interchangeable robots and N goals in planar environments with polygonal obstacles. After a conformal map to a circular domain, starts and goals become the poles and zeros of a rational function R, and the paths are the branches of its Generalized Root Locus (GRL), i.e. the streamlines of the logarithmic potential -log R. We show that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles; the robot-goal assignment is produced by the construction, and with the gain used as a clock all robots move as the closed-loop roots of the GRL and arrive together at a prescribed time. Obstacles become streamlines through successive Milne-Thomson reflections, and for a finite number of reflections a finite test certifies safety for the potential that is actually computed. Reciprocal root-locus planning is recovered as a special case. The method is illustrated on two polygonal workspaces, 100 random instances compared with independent harmonic planning and artificial potentials, and a scene with ten robots and ten obstacles.

papers.abstract_en: A $k$-path vertex cover ($k$-PVC) of a graph is a set of vertices meeting every path on $k$ vertices. In Token Sliding, one token occupies each vertex of a cover; a move slides one token along an edge to an unoccupied vertex, preserving the cover property. We study whether two covers of a tree are joined by such moves. The case $k=2$ admits a linear-time decision algorithm. For every integer $k\geq2$, we give an $O(kn^2)$-time decision algorithm on trees of order $n$, with $k$ part of the input. Two covers are reachable precisely when their rigid tokens, which never move, occupy the same set and every component remaining after their deletion has the same token count. The proof transforms configurations of equal size without rigid tokens into a canonical configuration built on properly rooted subtrees, whose paths on $k$ vertices pass through their roots. A rooted-subtree recurrence identifies movable candidate tokens. We also give a direct recursive construction between the supplied endpoints, returning at most $8n^2\,3^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$ slides in $O(n^{10}3^{n/2})$ time.   ChatGPT 6 Pro and Claude Fable 5.1 were used to assist with developing and reviewing mathematical arguments and drafting and revising the paper. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness and content of the paper.

papers.abstract_en: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.

papers.abstract_en: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well.   Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

papers.abstract_en: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $Θ_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $ψ^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Przeździecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

papers.abstract_en: For over two centuries, the esteemed mathematicians Gauss and Fourier conjectured that each real critical point of the rational function $p^{'}(s)/p(s)$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The conjecture remains unresolved. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are real multiple zero of $p^{'}(s)$ are defined as the second kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. In addition to the second kind of zeros, the other real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ are referred to as the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. We demonstrate that the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ emerge from the intersection of root loci emitted from non-real zeros of $p(s)$, thereby providing a comprehensive geometric interpretation of their relationship. Moreover, each first kind of zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is connected via root loci to a pair of conjugate non-real zeros of $p(s)$. This establishes the precise geometric relationship conjectured by Gauss and Fourier, fully resolving their original problem for first-kind zeros and completing a foundational chapter in polynomial theory. We have proven Gauss-Fourier conjecture about the first kind of zeros.

papers.abstract_en: We determine the zero-forcing number of maximal biconnected outerplanar graphs. When the weak dual is a path, the zero-forcing number and the induced path-covering number are both two. Otherwise, the branching faces determine a canonical core and a family of terminal strips. We prove that an optimal forcing process can be chosen in a normal form governed by explicit vertex and face capacities on the core. After fixing forests on the terminal strips, the zero-forcing number is expressed through an optimization over core-edge selections and the minimum number of root connections that must be removed to obtain an executable orientation. The path-covering number is obtained from the same capacity optimization without the repair cost. We characterize executable orientations by blocking-circuit equations and identify the two-path obstruction with a first cohomology class of a signed contact multigraph. Local replacements and a finite comparison of boundary recurrences establish the normal form for graphs of arbitrary size. A fifty-six-state recurrence constructs a minimum zero-forcing set and a complete forcing chronology in linear time from indexed triangle adjacency. We also obtain exact replacement results for rooted blocks and construct infinite families in which the zero-forcing number exceeds the path-covering number.

papers.abstract_en: Nuclear quantum effects can strongly influence excited-state processes involving light nuclei, yet their inclusion in practical molecular dynamics remains challenging. We develop constrained nuclear-electronic orbital time-dependent density functional theory (CNEO-TDDFT), which incorporates quantum-nuclear delocalization into full-dimensional effective excited-state potential energy surfaces while retaining the formal structure and computational scaling of conventional TDDFT. Analytic gradients are also developed, enabling efficient on-the-fly excited-state dynamics. CNEO-TDDFT substantially improves excited-state vibrational frequencies involving hydrogen motion and reduces the root-mean-square deviation from experiment from 113 cm$^{-1}$ to 26 cm$^{-1}$. For excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ), CNEO-TDDFT yields a characteristic transfer time of 14.0 fs, compared with 25.5 fs from conventional TDDFT, consistent with the experimentally inferred ultrafast timescale of 12$\pm$6 fs. These results establish CNEO-TDDFT as an accurate and efficient framework for excited-state dynamics with nuclear quantum effects.

papers.abstract_en: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the three-parameter $r$-largest generalized extreme-value ($r$GEV) model with a fixed number $r$ of upper order statistics per block. Because the support depends on all three parameters, the classical regular theory does not apply. We show that the maximum likelihood estimator is strongly consistent on compact parameter sets contained in $k<1$, where $k=-γ$ denotes the shape parameter. For $k_0<1/2$, the range in which the model is differentiable in quadratic mean, the estimator is root-$n$ consistent, asymptotically normal and asymptotically efficient. The proof verifies the conditions of the moving-support likelihood theorem of Bücher and Segers for the ordered $r$-dimensional likelihood; the main new ingredients are a sequential modified likelihood criterion and a support-loss bound showing that the regularity threshold $k_0<1/2$ does not depend on $r$. In simulated heavy-tailed cases with only $50$ blocks, using five to seven order statistics instead of the block maximum reduces the relative bias of the 100-year return level from $6$--$13\%$ to below $5\%$.

papers.abstract_en: The end-of-month option allows the short in a futures contract to choose when to deliver during a window in which the delivery price is fixed. We characterize optimal delivery through a universal index obtained from the Bank--El Karoui representation theorem. In the semimartingale setting, this is the Gittins index of holding the underlying and collecting its convenience yield, and the futures price is the retirement reward for which the value of this project equals the spot price. This characterization yields price bounds and a criterion for immediate delivery. Dinkelbach's iteration reduces the price computation to a sequence of standard optimal stopping problems, with an explicit contraction bound. We apply the theory to geometric Brownian motion and the Gibson--Schwartz model with stochastic convenience yield. For geometric Brownian motion, we characterize when the futures price equals spot and derive a square-root boundary asymptotic near expiry. For the Gibson--Schwartz model, we establish monotonicity in the yield and characterize the critical yield below which the price equals spot. Numerical results illustrate the price iteration and delivery regions.

papers.abstract_en: Sampling-based motion planning such as Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control has become attractive for robotics due to its ability to handle nonlinear dynamics and non-smooth objectives without gradient information, while leveraging parallel rollout computation for real-time performance. However, in real-world robotic systems, the optimized control input is often applied after a non-negligible planning delay, causing a mismatch between the state used in forward simulation and the actual state at control execution, which can significantly degrade planning accuracy and may even lead to unsafe behavior such as collisions. This paper proposes Closed-Loop MPPI with Initial-State Sampling (CLIS-MPPI), which explicitly addresses execution-time state mismatch by modeling planning delay as a distribution over plausible execution-time initial states, performing rollout optimization from sampled initial states, and applying a rollout-based local feedback correction during control execution. The proposed method is validated through real-world experiments on a 6-DoF UR5e manipulator in a narrow-passage task involving obstacle avoidance and end-effector target reaching. Across 5 real-world runs of the same task, standard MPPI collided in 2 runs, whereas CLIS-MPPI remained collision-free in all 5 runs. Averaged over all collision-free runs for each method (3 for MPPI and 5 for CLIS-MPPI), CLIS-MPPI reduced the average task completion time from 25.4s to 24.4s and the average end-effector path length from 0.456 m to 0.425 m. It also reduced the overall joint-position and joint-velocity root mean square errors (RMSEs) from 0.100 rad and 0.108 rad/s to 0.017 rad and 0.011 rad/s, respectively. These results demonstrate improved safety, planning-execution consistency, and motion smoothness.
